name: hazel_weir_central_procedural_graph
description: High-throughput Procedural Graph featuring Day 30 Town Shop arbitrage, cluster-harvesting transit efficiency, pre-planting fertilizer synchronization, capped 18-plot land expansion, and strict terminal crop maturation gating.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Computes net available cash, shed fill percentage, wage liability, active shop contract demand, and oracle price drop signals across market commodities.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Enforces dynamic cash reserve locks and triggers pre-midnight surplus liquidation to prevent the 0-hand bankruptcy cascade.

nodes.name: Town Shop Demand Arbitrage
nodes.description: Preemptively matches unlocked town shop demand surges and immediately fulfills mature high-margin crops (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins, Strawberries) to capture 2.0x-3.5x contract price premiums.

nodes.name: Shed Headroom Relief
nodes.description: Prevents silent 100/100 harvest discards by clearing uncommitted low-margin inventory under strict price floors while protecting animal feed and shop contracts.

nodes.name: Oracle Opponent Front-Run
nodes.description: Reads 96-step TTM forecast to dump sensitive commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) immediately before opponent market gluts collapse prices.

nodes.name: Capital Reinvestment & Yield Scaling
nodes.description: Reinvests surplus cash beyond wage reserves into workforce acceleration (10-hand rush), contiguous land expansion, commercial high-yield seeds, and fertilizer.

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Workforce Execution
nodes.description: Executes field routines with strict operational sequencing: harvest ready crops, worker drop-offs, watering, livestock feeding, planting, and ground maintenance.

attributes.guidance: Cancel non-essential purchases (BUY_SEED, BUY_ANIMAL, BUY_LAND, redundant HIRE); schedule worker harvest drop-offs before hour 21; enforce emergency liquidation of non-feed, non-contract inventory at hour >= 20 to guarantee midnight payroll.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve max(0, n_animals * 3); do not rely on low-margin fertilizer sales to cover payroll deficits; never liquidate crops committed to active town shop delivery.

attributes.guidance: Allocate up to 3 market slots to immediately deliver matching mature shed inventory directly to town shops through Day 30 to capture 2.0x-3.5x contract price premiums; procure shop-demanded seeds (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins) only when remaining contract duration strictly exceeds crop growth cycle time (Pumpkins <= Day 23, Tomatoes <= Day 25, Carrots <= Day 27) and surplus cash covers seed costs plus wage buffers.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not commit seed capital if net cash falls below 1.20x midnight payroll reserve; do not purchase shop seeds if remaining contract time is less than crop maturation duration; never allow shop-deliverable produce to be liquidated via routine market sales or shed headroom dumping.

attributes.guidance: Evict pending non-urgent buy orders to free order slots; monetize uncommitted surplus commodities (strictly excluding town shop commitments and livestock feed) when prices reach cyclical peaks (current_price >= 1.15 * base_price) capped at 1-2 open order slots to maintain a lean 40%-60% shed baseline; if shed capacity exceeds 80%, execute batch sales of unreserved surplus at price >= 0.85 * base_price, relaxing floor to 0.60 * base_price only if shed_used >= 95 to prevent silent discard drops.
attributes.pitfalls: Never fire-sell below 0.85x base price during transient shed spikes unless shed fill strictly exceeds 95%; never liquidate Wheat below dynamic feed reserve max(0, n_animals * 3); never evict or sell produce allocated for active town shop fulfillment.

attributes.condition: oracle_glut_risk >= 0.40 and current_price >= 0.85 * base_price and uncommitted_inventory > 0
attributes.guidance: Preempt lowest-margin open orders; execute rapid batch liquidations of uncommitted vulnerable commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) while current market price remains favorable (>= 0.85 * base_price) before opponent dumping collapses market prices.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not dump into already collapsed sub-0.60 base price markets unless shed overflow is imminent; do not front-run commodities committed to active town shop contracts; protect livestock feed reserve max(0, n_animals * 3).

attributes.condition: net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.20 + 130.0 and (hired_hands < 10 or (uncultivated_plots <= 1 and total_plots < 18) or has_fertilizer_deficit or (empty_cultivated_plots > 0 and day <= 28)) and day <= 28
attributes.guidance: Accelerate workforce expansion to the 10-hand cap with a balanced payroll safety buffer; expand contiguous land acreage up to 18 plots only when existing plots are fully cultivated; decouple continuous commercial seed procurement so empty cultivated plots are immediately replanted; enforce strict crop growth horizons: halt Pumpkin and Strawberry seed buying after Day 23, Tomatoes after Day 25, Carrots after Day 27, pivot to fast Wheat on Days 28-29, and cease all seed purchases by Day 29 noon.
attributes.pitfalls: Never allocate reinvestment capital if net cash after purchase drops below 1.15x midnight wage buffer; do not acquire land plots beyond 18 plots to prevent transit sprawl; never plant long-maturation crops after their cutoff days; halt hand and land expansion after Day 26 to maximize terminal cash accumulation.

attributes.guidance: Dispatch active hands strictly by operational priority: 1) Cluster harvesting: harvest adjacent ripe crops until worker carrying capacity is full before navigating to the shed for drop-off; 2) Drop off full carried inventory at shed; 3) Water dry crops to maintain maximum growth rate; 4) Apply fertilizer to tilled soil immediately prior to seeding; 5) Plant high-margin commercial seeds on fertilized plots; 6) Feed hungry livestock; 7) Weed clearing and ground tilling. On Days 29-30, redirect 100% of workforce away from tilling/planting to watering, harvesting, and shed drop-offs, depositing all carried items into shed by step 716 for final liquidation.
attributes.pitfalls: Never execute single-item shed drop-offs when adjacent ripe crops remain unharvested and carrying capacity permits; never plant seeds on unfertilized soil when fertilizer is available; never prioritize weeding over harvesting, watering, or fertilizing; ensure hands never idle while unharvested crops or dry plots remain.
